review.summary: AgentBench offers a useful, broad interactive benchmark spanning eight environments and evaluates 25 LLMs, providing a shared testbed and evidence of substantial variation in agent performance. Its breadth and release are valuable, though claims about practical capability depend on heterogeneous tasks and evaluation procedures, several of which use constructed or automated judging. This assessment inspected the introduction, portions of the task protocols, and conclusion/results snippets rather than the complete paper.

observations.claim: The benchmark contributes breadth by combining newly created and adapted settings rather than evaluating agents in only one environment.
observations.quote: AgentBench encompasses 8 distinct environments, 5 of which are created in this paper for the first time

observations.claim: The reported evaluation compares a substantial set of API and open models, with GPT-4 leading across most task datasets.
observations.quote: gpt-4 presents the best performance on 7 out of 8 datasets in AgentBench

observations.claim: At least one task setting simplifies its underlying game, so results in that environment do not directly establish performance in the more complex original game.
observations.quote: The original design of Aquawar could be too complicated for existing LLMs.

observations.claim: Lateral-puzzle results rely on an automated GPT-3.5 host and judging procedures; the inspected passages do not establish how robust these measures are to evaluator errors or prompt choices.
observations.quote: we first design an accurate LTP host system based on gpt-3.5-turbo for automatic game playing

unresolved_questions: How stable are model rankings across repeated runs, prompt variants, and updates to API models?
How sensitive are aggregate scores to the chosen weighting across environments and task-specific metrics?

I inspected only selected pages and search excerpts, not all environment protocols, result analyses, or appendices; further claims about reproducibility, task validity, and detailed statistical uncertainty remain unassessed.
